title: Long and short stitch
subtitle: An alternating stitch fill used for smooth tonal shading
excerpt: Long and short stitch fills shapes with alternating long and short stitches that interlock between rows, allowing colours to blend smoothly. It is the primary shading stitch in crewelwork and silk embroidery, used wherever a gradual tonal transition is needed.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), shading stitch chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 4 (1888), long and short shading entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The second and subsequent rows of long and short stitch, where new stitches are split into the ends of the previous row to create a smooth tonal blend.

heroPrompt: Long and short stitch filling a large petal with three tones of pink shading from deep at the base to pale at the tip, on cream linen, natural light.

content.text: Long and short stitch builds tonal shading through

that interlock with the previous colour. The first row at the edge of a shape alternates long and short stitches. Subsequent rows split into the ends of the previous row so no hard line shows between colours.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 strands in three to four tonal shades

content.text: Work split stitch around the shape outline. This raises the edge and defines where the first long and short row meets the border.
Work the first row at the shape edge: alternate a long stitch (6 to 8 mm) and a short stitch (3 to 4 mm) all the way across.
For row two in the next colour, bring the needle up in the body of the previous row and split down through the ends of the short stitches. All stitches in this row are the same length.
Continue with each new colour, splitting into the row before. The colours blend where the stitches interlock.

attrs.heading: When long and short stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: A hard line of colour shows between rows
items.cause: Row two is not splitting far enough into row one.
items.fix: The new stitches must travel past the end of the previous-row stitches, not just meet them. Split 2 to 3 mm inside the previous row.

items.symptom: The stitches splay out of parallel
items.cause: Following the shape outline rather than keeping stitches parallel.
items.fix: All stitches in a shape run at the same angle regardless of the shape edge. The edge of the shape is followed by the stitch length, not the stitch direction.

content.text: Long and short stitch is the primary shading technique of crewelwork, needlepainting, and Chinese silk embroidery. The interlocking row principle also appears in brick stitch and encroaching satin stitch.
